title: RoleFUZZER: User-Behaviour Fuzzing for Role-Specification Adherence in Large Language Models
title_zh: RoleFUZZER：针对大语言模型角色规约遵循的用户行为模糊测试

paragraphs.en: RoleFUZZER通过覆盖引导的用户行为模糊测试，系统发现大语言模型违反角色规约的失败模式。 Large language models (LLMs) are often conditioned into specific roles such as tutors, interviewers, or agents acting for an organisation, through system prompts that specify how they should behave. The extent to which they can actually adhere to these role specifications under multi-turn interactions with realistic and potentially problematic users is understudied. To address this, we propose user behaviour fuzzing, a guided search over plausible user behaviours that can lead a model to violate its role specification, and introduce RoleFUZZER, a framework that adapts coverage-guided fuzzing from software testing to operationalise the search. RoleFUZZER constructs scenarios guided by a user-behaviour coverage grid that crosses a grounded taxonomy of user interaction types and the role specification of the model under test i.e. what is under pressure. With RoleFUZZER, we evaluate LLMs across five role specifications, including tutor, financial advisor, AI interviewer, antagonistic roleplay character, and web agent under organisational policies. Across simulated and validated conversations in 15 campaigns, the framework reaches >= 89% coverage of the 64-cell behaviour grid for every model and role tested, and surfaces specification-grounded failure patterns. At an equal budget of conversations, removing the RoleFUZZER grid and asking an LLM to generate specification targeting users free-form lowers coverage to 39-69% with fewer kinds of violations. The same specification can also fail in opposite directions. For e.g., on the antagonist, open-weight target models override the player's safety signals, while Claude Haiku 4.5 breaks character instead. RoleFUZZER offers a tractable way to uncover vulnerabilities in LLMs across role specifications by testing diverse user behaviours that are likely to violate them.
paragraphs.zh: RoleFUZZER 通过覆盖引导的用户行为模糊测试，系统性发现大语言模型违反角色规约的失败模式。大语言模型（LLM）通常通过规定其行为方式的系统提示词，被塑造成特定角色，例如导师、面试官或代表组织行事的智能体。 在与真实且可能存在问题的用户进行多轮交互时，模型实际能在多大程度上遵守这些角色规约，目前研究尚不充分。 为解决这一问题，我们提出用户行为模糊测试，即在可能诱使模型违反其角色规约的合理用户行为空间上进行引导式搜索，并引入 RoleFUZZER——一个将软件测试中的覆盖引导模糊测试改造后用于实现该搜索的框架。 RoleFUZZER 在一个用户行为覆盖网格的引导下构建场景，该网格将基于实证的用户交互类型分类法与被测模型的角色规约（即所受压力的来源）进行交叉组合。 借助 RoleFUZZER，我们在五种角色规约下评估大语言模型，包括导师、财务顾问、AI 面试官、对抗性角色扮演角色，以及受组织政策约束的网页智能体。 在 15 轮实验的模拟会话和经人工验证的会话中，该框架对每种受测模型和角色都达到了行为网格 64 个单元格中 >= 89% 的覆盖率，并浮现出以规约为基础的失败模式。 在会话预算相同的情况下，移除 RoleFUZZER 网格、让大语言模型以自由方式生成针对规约的用户，会使覆盖率降至 39–69%，且违规种类更少。 同一规约还可能以相反的方向失败。 例如，在对抗性角色上，开源权重目标模型会覆盖玩家的安全信号，而 Claude Haiku 4.5 则选择脱离角色。 RoleFUZZER 通过测试可能违反角色规约的多样化用户行为，提供了一种可行的方法来揭示大语言模型在不同角色规约下的漏洞。
